_README: D&D 4e has NO open-content release. The Game System License forbade reproducing rules
text, tables and even monster stat blocks, the 4e 'SRD' was only an index of terms and
templates rather than the rules, and the GSL is no longer offered. So unlike pf2e.py
(ORC) and dnd5e.py (CC-BY-4.0), this framework CANNOT ship 4e's numeric tables.
Every value below is null until YOU type it in from books you own. The tools refuse to
compute rather than guessing: an unfilled table produces an error naming the table and
where to read it, not a plausible number.
python3 tools/dnd4e.py tables      # what is filled and what is not
python3 tools/dnd4e.py sources     # the provenance discipline for this ruleset
Fill only what you need. A campaign that never leaves the heroic tier needs levels 1-10
of three tables and nothing else. `tables --missing` lists what the command you just ran
This file is yours. It holds values transcribed from your own books for your own use,
and it is listed in .gitignore's spirit if you would rather not commit it — see

character_xp._source: Player's Handbook, the Character Advancement table — the cumulative XP to reach each level
character_xp._note: Fill as far as your campaign will reach. Level 1 is 0.

monster_xp_by_level._source: Monster Manual / Dungeon Master's Guide, the Experience Point Rewards table
monster_xp_by_level._shape: monster level (1-33) -> XP for a standard monster of that level
monster_xp_by_level._note: Standard monsters only. The role multipliers go in `monster_role_multipliers`.

monster_role_multipliers._source: Dungeon Master's Guide, how elite, solo and minion monsters count against a budget
monster_role_multipliers._shape: role -> multiplier applied to the standard XP for that level

encounter_budget_per_character._source: Dungeon Master's Guide, building an encounter — the XP budget for one character of a given level
encounter_budget_per_character._shape: party level (1-30) -> XP budget per character for a standard encounter
encounter_budget_per_character._note: 4e's standard encounter is level-appropriate by default; difficulty is usually tuned by raising or lowering the encounter's level relative to the party rather than by a separate budget column. If your books give difficulty columns, use `encounter_budget_columns` instead and leave this null.

encounter_budget_columns._source: Dungeon Master's Guide, if your printing gives more than one difficulty column
encounter_budget_columns._shape: difficulty name -> {party level -> XP budget per character}

dc_by_level._source: Rules Compendium or DMG, the Difficulty Class by Level table. NOTE this table was REVISED by errata — check which printing you are using and record it in `_printing` below

treasure_parcels._source: Dungeon Master's Guide, the treasure parcels for a level
treasure_parcels._shape: level (1-30) -> a list of parcel descriptions, each a string you write
treasure_parcels._note: 4e hands out treasure as a numbered set of parcels per level rather than a lump sum. Transcribe the parcel list for the levels you are running, or write your own and say so.

magic_item_prices._source: Player's Handbook / Adventurer's Vault, the Magic Item Prices by Level table
magic_item_prices._shape: item level (1-30) -> market price in gp

monster_benchmarks._source: Dungeon Master's Guide, the monster statistics by level table
monster_benchmarks._shape: level -> {ac, fortitude, reflex, will, hp_per_level, attack, damage}
monster_benchmarks._note: Only needed if you build monsters from benchmarks rather than using published ones. A published monster's own stat block is always preferred — see rule 4 of the charter.
